description: Impairment profiles for the user-space UDP relay of mission M38 (host/impair/impair_proxy.py). Every impairment is applied between the real bench processes; the decisions are a pure function of (seed, direction, datagram index). NOT a kernel impairment: see docs/NETWORK-IMPAIRMENT.md for the tc/netem recipe (not executed here) and for the limits.

profiles.name: nominal
profiles.description: Control run: the relay forwards every datagram untouched. Same topology, same wiring, zero impairment.

profiles.name: loss-1pct
profiles.description: Uniform random loss, 1 % of the datagrams, in every direction.

profiles.name: loss-10pct
profiles.description: Uniform random loss, 10 % of the datagrams, in every direction.

profiles.name: burst-gilbert
profiles.description: Burst loss, Gilbert-Elliott two-state chain in every direction. Mean stay in the good state 1/0.01 = 100 datagrams, mean burst 1/0.25 = 4 datagrams lost at 95 %: longer than the patience p = 3, so mandates must be revoked on the actuator's own evidence.

profiles.name: reorder-deep
profiles.description: Deep reordering in every direction: a hold buffer of depth 8 releases a random buffered datagram when full, and flushes anything held for more than 60 ms. No loss, no delay: only the order changes.

profiles.name: delay-50ms-asym
profiles.description: Asymmetric delay: the orders (node to actuator) take 50 ms plus or minus 5 ms, two ticks at T = 25 ms, so they reach the actuator with a stale tick label; the STATUT way back and the peer links stay clean.

profiles.name: duplicate-5pct
profiles.description: Duplication: 5 % of the datagrams are sent twice in every direction, the copy 12 ms behind the original, so it lands in the next tick with a stale label.

profiles.name: corrupt-2pct
profiles.description: Byte corruption: 2 % of the datagrams get 1 or 2 bits flipped in every direction. The CRC-32C and the SipHash MAC of the frame must catch every one of them (SEC-01, DET-04).

profiles.name: truncate-2pct
profiles.description: Truncation: 2 % of the datagrams are cut to a random length of at least 8 bytes in every direction. A short frame must be rejected, never applied.

profiles.name: blackout-orders
profiles.description: The network is too bad to command: every datagram from a node to the actuator is lost (100 %), the STATUT and the peer links stay clean. No mandat can live; the actuator must serve the fallback law and light the lamp, without ever applying a value nobody ordered.
